hints.S15_A1: The comparison is a BEEHIVE, and everyone is BUZZING with ideas. Ask: is a beehive still and empty, or packed with movement and work? Match the adjective to the hive, not to the temperature of the room.
hints.S15_A2: The clue is FROM BOOKS AND THE INTERNET - facts are being brought together from several places. Ask: which verb means to collect things from different sources? 'Invent' makes facts up, and 'ignore' and 'forget' throw them away.
hints.S15_A3: The clue is PUT IT AWAY NEATLY after the experiment - the mess must be removed and the equipment tidied. Ask: which phrasal verb means to tidy a place? 'Break down' means stop working, and 'give in' means surrender.
hints.S15_A4: They HUGGED AND CHEERED after winning FIRST PLACE. Ask: does the idiom describe the highest joy, or illness, or trouble, or confusion? An idiom cannot be read word by word - learn the whole phrase.
hints.S15_A5: They had to COMPLETE THEIR MODEL before the DEADLINE, so what did the class pour into the task? Ask: which choice is something you actually give to a job - not 'noise', not 'rest', not 'argument'?
hints.S15_B1: The subject is NOBODY, not 'the class'. Words like nobody and everyone act like ONE person. Ask: in the present tense, does a singular subject take the plain verb, or the verb ending in -s?
hints.S15_B2: HAS is already sitting in the sentence, so the blank must partner with it. Ask: after 'has', do we need the plain verb, the -s form, the -ing form, or the past participle? Only one of them builds a present perfect.
hints.S15_B3: The PRINCIPAL WALKED IN suddenly, cutting across an action that had already started. Ask: which choice shows a past action still going on when something else interrupted it? A plain past verb only reports a finished action.
hints.S15_B4: THAN tells you two models are being compared, and this adjective is a long one. Ask: do long adjectives take -er, or do they need a comparing word placed in front? 'Most' is for three or several, and 'impressiver' is not English.
hints.S15_B5: Being ABSENT FROM SCHOOL is the reason he missed the test, not the result of it. Ask: which joining word introduces a reason? 'So' would put the result in the wrong half, and 'although' signals a contrast.
hints.S15_B6: A tag mirrors the main verb, and the statement uses WAS. Ask: after a positive statement, does the tag turn negative or stay positive? And should it keep the same verb rather than borrow 'did'?
hints.S15_B7: The blank sits right in front of the noun PROJECT, so it must show who the project belongs to. Ask: can a subject pronoun like 'they' or an object pronoun like 'them' describe a noun? 'Theirs' must stand alone.
hints.S15_B8: The sentence looks back at a finished event: the project WAS DIFFICULT. Ask: should the second verb match that past time, or stay in the present? This verb is regular, so it takes the ordinary past ending.
hints.S15_C1: The verb in front of the blank is ENJOYS. Ask: after enjoy, does English take the plain verb, the infinitive, or the -ing form? Enjoy is one of the verbs that accepts only a gerund.
hints.S15_C2: EVERY NIGHT signals a repeated habit, so the tense stays present - and the subject is SHE, one person. Ask: does a singular subject take the plain verb, or the one that ends in -s?
hints.S15_C3: LAST WEEK puts this firmly in finished time. Ask: what is the past form of this verb? It is irregular, so it never takes -ed - the form 'writed' does not exist in English.
hints.S15_C4: WHILE SHE marks a long background action that another event cut across: the teacher CALLED HER NAME. Ask: which form shows an action still in progress in the past? A plain past verb would only show it finished.
hints.S15_C5: THE OTHER STUDENTS are plural, and they act AT THE SAME TIME as everything else. Ask: which past form shows several people in the middle of an action? Match the helping verb to a plural subject.
hints.S15_C6: 'Reminded us' comes first, and that pattern needs an infinitive after its object. Ask: after 'reminded us', do you use the -ing form, the bare verb alone, or the infinitive with its little particle in front?
hints.S15_C7: SHOULD belongs with the modal family, and modals never allow an ending on the verb that follows. Ask: after should, must or can, do you add -s, add -ing, or leave the verb completely bare?
hints.S15_C8: RIGHT NOW points at this very moment, and MY FRIEND counts as one person. Ask: which form shows an action happening as we speak? A plain present verb would only describe a habit.
hints.S15_D1: The blank is followed BY READING BOOKS AND WATCHING VIDEOS online - that tells you how the group dug into the topic. Ask: which box word is a past verb meaning to look into a subject and collect facts?
hints.S15_D2: It comes BEFORE WRITING THE FINAL REPORT, and the teacher checks it first. Ask: which box word names an early version of a piece of writing that can still be changed? A 'deadline' is a date, not a version.
hints.S15_D3: The teacher is POINTING OUT AREAS that need more detail, so the students can improve. Ask: which box word names the helpful comments a teacher gives on your work? The blank follows 'useful', so it is a noun.
hints.S15_D4: The students MADE CHANGES so that no errors would be left in their reports. Ask: which box word means correct and free of mistakes? 'Confusing' is the opposite of what a good report should be.
hints.S15_D5: The clue is USING POSTERS AND A SHORT TALK in front of the class. Ask: which box word is a past verb meaning to show and explain your work to an audience? 'Borrowed' takes something away instead.
hints.S15_E1: The sentence is about the EXCITEMENT reaching you through your ears, not about a place. Ask: does the underlined word mean 'at this spot', or does it belong to your ears? One of the two spellings has EAR inside it.
hints.S15_E2: BEGINNED has been built with the regular -ed rule, but this verb refuses that rule. Ask: how would you say it about yesterday - 'the group ___ mixing'? Strong verbs change their vowel instead of taking an ending.
hints.S15_E3: CUTTED copies the regular -ed pattern onto a verb that will not accept it. Ask: does this verb change at all in the past, or does it keep exactly the same shape, like 'put' and 'hit'?
hints.S15_E4: Find the real subject: THE SUPPLIES - more than one thing. Ask: does a plural subject take the singular form of 'to be', or the plural one? Match the verb to the subject noun, not to the nearest word.
hints.S15_E5: The COMMENTS belong to the TEACHERS, and there are several of them. Ask: does a plain -s show ownership, or does it only make a plural? Where must the apostrophe go when the owners are more than one person?
hints.S15_F1: A yes/no question turned into REPORTED SPEECH. Ask three things: which small joining word follows 'asked'? Does the question keep its question order, or switch to statement order? And what happens to 'you' and to 'have'?
hints.S15_F2: One action was already running when the other suddenly happened. Ask: which sentence gives the long background action, and which gives the sudden one? Keep 'WERE' in the background half and put 'when' before the sudden event.
